## TL;DR
RepoOS now guards against huge and build-output files and secrets in WIP checkpoint commits and branch diffs: path and size rules, a bounded secret scan that decompresses gzip, zlib and zstd, a check-gate step, and a pre-commit hook on every branch. DerivedData now lives outside the repo. This round fixes review pass 7.

## Work and rationale
- `.github/workflows/macos-hub.yml`: the Package DMG step still read `macos/.derived-data/Build/Products/Release/RepoOS Hub.app`, but the release build writes to `$REPOOS_MACOS_DERIVED_DATA` (under `runner.temp`), so DMG packaging would have failed on every tag release. It now uses the same variable (a job-level env, already set for the whole job). A repo-wide search found no other reference to the old in-repo path in this diff's scope.
- The `repoos.toml` Hub dev command (`macos/.derived-data/...`, line 745) has the same stale path. Config never lands with a task, so the one-line change is applied on main at sign-off: the command should derive `${REPOOS_MACOS_DERIVED_DATA:-$HOME/Library/Caches/RepoOS/macos-derived-data}` like `just macos-build`.
- Earlier rounds on the branch stay: blob-only reads, HEAD content scan, bounded inflation, gzip trailing bytes, windowed large-file scan, shared allowlist-aware scan, whole-buffer raw scan, refusal unstaging, narrower hook exemption, renames, deletions, bounded directory walk.

## Approaches tried
Pointing the workflow at the env var rather than hard-coding a second path, so the build and package steps cannot drift apart again.

## Challenges and blockers
The workflow change cannot be exercised locally; it is a one-variable swap of the path the same job already uses at the build and verify steps.

## Key learnings
When a build output path moves, grep for every consumer (dev target, workflow, scripts), not just the producer.
